report:
**Conclusion**
The health claim is **true**. Robust clinical trial evidence confirms that the adjuvanted recombinant zoster vaccine (RZV, marketed as Shingrix) significantly reduces the incidence of shingles (herpes zoster) in adults aged 70 years or older.

**Evidence Summary**
1. **High Clinical Efficacy (ZOE-70 Trial):** The Phase 3 randomized, placebo-controlled ZOE-70 trial evaluated RZV specifically in adults aged 70 years and older. Findings demonstrated high efficacy, with the vaccine proving roughly 89.8% to 91% effective at preventing shingles in this age group (https://www.pharmacytimes.com/view/4-things-pharmacists-should-know-about-the-shingrix-vaccine, https://shingrixhcp.com/efficacy-safety/efficacy-data/).
2. **Reduction in Shingles and Complications:** Pivotal study results published in the *New England Journal of Medicine* verified that RZV reduces the risks of both herpes zoster and its primary complication, postherpetic neuralgia, among individuals 70 years of age or older (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27626517/).
3. **Public Health Guidelines:** Based on these efficacy findings, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) recommends RZV for immunocompetent adults aged 50 years and older, noting there is no maximum age limit (https://www.cdc.gov/shingles/hcp/vaccine-considerations/index.html).

**Sources**
* https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27626517/
* https://www.pharmacytimes.com/view/4-things-pharmacists-should-know-about-the-shingrix-vaccine
* https://shingrixhcp.com/efficacy-safety/efficacy-data/
* https://www.cdc.gov/shingles/hcp/vaccine-considerations/index.html
